text: Jacek Karpiński was born in 1927 in Turin, Italy, into a family of Polish intellectuals and alpinists. His father, Adam Karpiński, was an aeronautic engineer and inventor, while his mother, Wanda Czarnocka-Karpińska, was a respected physician. The family moved to Warsaw in 1934. Karpiński joined the Gray Ranks during World War II, serving in the Home Army and participating in numerous field operations, including the Warsaw Uprising. After the war, he attended local high school and later studied at the Warsaw University of Technology, where he graduated in 1951. He worked at the Polish Academy of Sciences' Institute of Basic Problems, where he developed the AAH — Analytical Analyzer of Harmonics. In 1959, he co-developed AKAT-1, the world's first differential equations analyzer based on transistors, which was praised for its aesthetic design. In 1960, he was awarded the UNESCO scholarship in the United States to visit major technological centers. After returning, he designed the perceptron, a device inspired by Frank Rosenblatt's ideas. In 1965, he designed the KAR-65, a computer used for data analysis. In 1970, he founded the Microcomputers' Construction Plant (Zakład Budowy Mikrokomputerów) to develop the K-202 minicomputer, though the project was not commercially successful. Karpiński later moved to Switzerland and returned to Poland in the 1990s. He was awarded the Officer's Cross of Polonia Restituta in 2009 and posthumously received the Commander's Cross of Polonia Restitutua in 2010. He died on 21 February 2010 in Wrocław.
